messages:
ana: Heads-up — noticing a new spike in console slow renders after the 06:00 deploy. Charts hang for ~3s on initial paint on big org pages. Anyone else seeing it?
sam: yep saw it in Sentry around 06:12. Lots of long tasks ~2000-3000ms main-thread. traces: https://sentry.redwood/issue/12345
lee: Interesting — metric and heatmap endpoints report normal latencies. Suspect client-side bundle or KV prefetch behavior changed.
irene: I rolled the prefetch priority tweak (PR #482) to canary last night; it changes how we fall through to prefix-kv cache when route mismatch. Could be related.
matt: Can we get a full flamegraph? main-thread shows heavy time in parse/compile for vendor chunk and inlined telemetry client.
nana (typo but let's keep consistent): :grimacing: whoops — meant ana.
nana: adding flametrace: `profile-06-12.html` — large parse spike, repeated rehydration of chart components.
sam: Also seeing a lot of network re-requests for tile data: repeated `GET /v1/console/metrics?tile=...` with identical params. Might be prefetch missing and then re-fetch.
lee: That matches a prefetch fallthrough loop — if KV prefetch returns miss, client retries fetch and triggers re-render. The change in PR #482 reduced prefetch TTL maybe causing more misses.
irene: PR #482 was supposed to avoid overfetching on route changes by lowering prefetch affinity. It passed unit tests. Didn't anticipate cascade effect on large dashboards.
frontend-oncall: We should consider rolling back canary for safety. What's the error budget hit?
matt: User impact 0.8% p95 up on large orgs. Not huge but visible to customers. I'd prefer to hotfix — revert prefetch policy or add a debounce around re-fetch.
nana: Quick mitigation: patch to gate re-fetch if an identical request is inflight. Small change in client request dedupe. I can make a PR.
sam: Good plan. Also we should instrument `prefetch_hit` / `prefetch_miss` events with `route_id` and `kv_key` so we can see which keys are thrashing. Right now telemetry is aggregated.
irene: I'll add telemetry fields and extend retention for the next 24h. Canary group still small, so we can validate.
deploy-bot: deploy-bot: canary deployment of `console-client@canary-482` started at 06:00 by @irene — pods: 4 -> 8 in EU and US.
lee: Another quick note — vendor chunk parsing dominating on mobile too because chunk split point changed in the build; we also had a new intl chunk inlined for charts. Could be two simultaneous regressions (prefetch + bundle churn).
matt: Ugh. Those split changes were from the deps bump to `viz-lib@2.3.1`. Maybe we should pin viz-lib while we triage.
nana: PR #490 created: `client: dedupe concurrent tile fetches + backoff` — simple mutex per-key. Testing locally replicates the loop and fixes it.
nana: example fix snippet:
```
// pseudo
if (inflight[key]) return await inflight[key]
inflight[key] = fetchTile(key)
try { return await inflight[key] } finally { delete inflight[key] }
```
irene: Nice. Can we add a guard to not cancel on route changes for 200ms (debounce window) to avoid immediate re-fetches?
sam: That plus telemetry will show whether misses spike because of TTL.
frontend-oncall: Recommend merging #490 to canary and watching p95 for next 30m. If no regressions, roll to stable. If still high, rollback #482 and pin viz-lib.
matt: I'll open a follow-up to pin viz-lib and revert the chunk split temp change.
deploy-bot: deploy-bot: canary deployment `console-client@canary-490` started at 06:34 by @ana — pods: 4 -> 8 in EU and US.
lee: After canary-490, observed prefetch miss rate drop from 42% -> 6% in 10m in EU. Main-thread long tasks reduced by ~60%.
irene: Great signal. Keep telemetry retention extended for 6h. I will prepare a rollback plan for #482 just in case.
sam: Also adding a small perf test to CI that simulates large dashboard load with route churn. If it fails, block merges to canary.
nana: I'll follow up with a short note in all-hands tomorrow about the subtle risk of prefetch affinity changes.
frontend-oncall: Thanks everyone — leaving monitoring alerts on. Ping here before rolling to stable. :thumbsup:
